item.title: SCP Idea, Seeking Concept Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Page type: New SCP idea
So my SCP is a man in a hot air balloon that is designated safe as he doesn't attack anything. The Hot-Air balloon itself can reach up to extremely fast speeds and stop on a time and do things such as move in any direction or things like barrel rolls. A real physics breaking type entity. For example, the Balloon can easily reach Mach 3 and then stop instantly with no inertia, no drag, nothing and the man in said balloon doesn't fly out of the balloon or do any type of bracing for the oncoming stop. The SCP itself can initiate maneuvers such as barrel rolls.

From what I read I have to get the concept greenlight then the draft and then the final green light for it to become and "Canon" article.

item.title: Re: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
I'm not a woman and I am fairly offended at this… so I would worry about anyone who identifies as female and how they might feel. Echoing all of the concerns mentioned above… I would also like to point out that the horrible misogyny angle of common horror tropes is not only offensive, it's boring.

Try to aim for something not meant to shock… because often times when we try to shock, we aim too low and end up writing offensive things… or more often, just boring things.

Think about something that makes you uneasy, and write an article about that, in a grounded contemplative way.

I would hope you are going to go back to the drawing board, but I just wanted to urge you to think about how others might respond to your proposal for the next idea.

item.title: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Exploration, Ambiance

Page Layout: Standard SCP Article with Explorations Logs towards the "doors"

Elevator Pitch: it revolves around a building called Lawang Sewu, a colonial-era building that has a thousand doors because it really does have lots of doors in it. Every door has its own theme about Colonialism History, the upper place or the ground floor is accessible by a tourist, but the underground section of the floor is forbidden by the public, and the whole building itself should be monitored and staffed with Foundation Guards.

Central Narrative: The narrative will focus on the exploration logs about these "doors" that are in the underground, at first it will be a normal abandoned underground room with an 1800-1900s theme, as the exploration goes deeper, it will get an even weirder and darker theme of the place itself, some of it may cause cognitive disturbances, and some may have an entity that is hostile and non-hostile. The Exploration team must explore the room to progress further into another room, the room itself appears to be not in order which results in every room they encounter is randomized every time they started the exploration.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Every room has its own theme, it tells how dark and cruel the colonization was. Tourists on the upper floor may see that colonization improved the country by a lot but in the underground, it tells the horrifying experience of being dictated by the upper echelon of that time. Tortured, discriminated, killed, etc by the colony. The Room expresses how the people back then were mistreated, some of the entities in the room being hostile because of it. The Foundation is still exploring the underground to know what really happened.

Additional Notes: I may add exploration logs also with some interviews with a non-hostile entity in the room to get a grasp of what does this room feels and its entity around it.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Twist is surrounded in what he calls a “LLUN” aura, which gives Twist his anomalous nature and various abilities and is what prevents Twist from speaking certain truths.

Sorry to be blunt, but what does this mean? I kept thinking it would get unpacked in one of the other sections but it doesn't.

Moreover, I don't see a connection between this aspect, the "deep secret" and the whole vaccine thing… Feels like a few thin ideas sorta slammed together without connective tissue.

James Devillian Twist will instantly uncover this kind of information simply by looking at these creatures. Twist will instantly know various bits of information about a target within his line of sight such as the target's purpose(supposed destiny), function, how it works, and how to eliminate it.

I assume this is from the Aura but that isn't any better connected to these other factors I mentioned above. I think you need to sit down and simplify, make a cohesive anomaly about the one man and focus on his anomalous aspects that thematically connect to each other.

Mostly I think this person's anomalous abilities aren't super interesting (knowing someone's destiny? What does that mean?) but primarily you need to make these different concepts work together or snip some of them.

My suggestion would be to cut the "vaccine" bit as it sounds a little too like SCP-049 without much to differentiate it.

item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

The SCP is motivated by a zealous belief that a K-class scenario is coming soon, though it doesn't know when or how, and the details it describes do not match any known K-class scenarios.

I really like this idea of reading the bones but I am unconvinced about the entire thing centered around a vague K-class event. That's no way to build stakes.

I think this could work without the vague threat, make it something a bit more grounded… like the Seer is worried about being hunted by something or someone (but don't be vague, be mysterious), while you sell it with how upset/scared they are and are looking for security in containment. (this is just an idea, you don't have to take the suggestion of course)

This belief does however leave it completely cold and apathetic to individual lives, including its own, as well as highly cooperative with the Foundation, believing it will be necessary to try and piece the world together after the cataclysm.

also not convinced that being sure the world would end would then lead to these results… like maybe the cooperation, but why would it make the SCP apathetic about the individual lives? That's fine if you wanna make them cold towards individual lives, but it doesn't make much sense this would be the reason personally.

can then turn to the experiment logs to see how various test subjects deal with having the memories of others

Also not really sold on this idea, I don't think experiment logs is the way to go here. Instead you could summarize what research was done with the results and then unpack them in conversations or observation reports from the researchers.

Overall, I like the idea of the core anomaly… but I think some unpacking of the actual anomaly would be more interesting than the focus on some vague end of the world. Most of the compelling SCPs I have read have not had such HUGE stakes. I think this would work better with a more grounded relatable story about a person who can see into weird shit and how its affected them… Maybe some of the history of the practice, where this person has been/where they've used it before, and some unpacking of their psychological status as a result.

item.title: SCP-XXXX (Veracity)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Technical SCP including developments associated with the testing of this SCP. Focus on addendums and Incident Reports to describe the Foundation’s efforts to contain and understand this object.

+ Elevator Pitch:
– hide block

Elevator Pitch:
Foundation Discovery of GRU-P Experiments at New Research Area Kantubek located on the Vozdrozhdeniya Isthmus (Formerly island) in the now diminishing Aral Sea region near the Kazakhstan/Uzbekistan border. SCP-XXXX is a Polygraph machine with cognitohazardous properties which affect those exposed to the results produced by the machine making them believe with certainty and without question the accuracy and truth of statements analyzed by the machine, even when presented with factual evidence to the contrary (cognitive dissonance). Further experimentation reveals additional congnitohazards associated with the machine as well as evidence of suspected retrocausal effects generated by the machine. Much of the story development in the article will occur via incident reports filed by Foundation personnel.

+ Central Narrative:
– hide block

Central Narrative:
SCP-XXXX is one of many SCPs the Foundation currently contains (or is attempting to contain) at Research Area Kantubek, formerly a GRU-P research and development facility. Central tension focuses around GRU-P mismanagement of anomalous items and persons and the implications of containment breaches. I would like to expand the story of SCP’s at Research Area Kantubek as well as create a number of tales which describe the lives and personal experiences of Foundation Personnel working within this former GRU-P compound. While this article is just to begin seeding plot ideas and characters regarding this small-ish setting, I would like to develop it into a larger series spanning around 20-25 years of Foundation efforts occurring at this area as well as their interactions with other GOI’s (and the associated physical, emotional and political challenges Foundation Personnel face here).

+ Hook/Attention-Grabber:
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Focus on a relatively mundane object which is discovered to have exceptional properties beyond original Foundation expectations and the Foundations scramble to expand Special Containment Procedures.

+ Additional Notes:
– hide block

Additional Notes:
I’d like this article to be both enjoyable as a stand-alone read as well as effectively seed interest in the wider story regarding SCPs and Foundation Personnel at RA-Kantubek. I don’t want the first piece to be of too grand a scale as to overshadow future pieces, but it also needs to be involved enough as to hint at other developments and stories in RA-Kantubek. I’m also concerned about writing something too “big”, but I’m not sure how much content should be in a single SCP article to retain interest but also to decently seed plot points for future articles. Any input and feedback is welcome and appreciated!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
EDIT: Formatting updates per comments from Zyn. ~Archivist 346

item.title: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded:
+Overall Thoughts
– hide block

Overall, I thought it was alright. You were worried about your dialogue, but it seemed fine to me (however, I'm not the best with dialogue, so you should definitely get a second opinion).

My first main concern is that you didn't cite your image. First, check the image use guidelines and make sure that your image is CC compliant. If it is, put a license box at the bottom of the page. If it isn't, you can't use it in your article. If you want to know where to find CC compliant images, I would recommend Wikimedia Commons and CCSearch.

My second issue are the test logs. The focus of your is on Licht's character arc, but your logs are pretty detached from that. You can also cut down on the description of SCP-####-A through -I by having there only be one button that lets Licht move outside of the flow of time, and then just letting him walk around outside of time instead of using multiple other buttons to do so.

+line-by-line
– hide block

SCP-#### has the ability to create a temporal anomaly capable of consuming the time of macroscopic life

"consuming time" is pretty vague. You explain the effect of this later in the paragraph, but I think you should find a better descriptor for the SCP's effect.

The activation time is inconsistent, along with the amount of time SCP-#### consumes.

I'd change this to "Both the activation time and the amount of time SCP-#### consumes1 are inconsistent."

SCP-#### appears to be designed to permanently attach itself to an humanoid individual. The requirements for this process to occur are as of yet unknown. It is also unknown if it is possible to remove SCP-#### without physically damaging the individual which it has attached to.

This makes it sound like SCP-#### is physically attached to an individual, when the recovery log shows that it just floats near them.

extreme gravitational lensing

I'd put a footnote briefly defining "gravitational lensing", since I imagine most readers won't know what that is (or maybe everyone knows what that is and it's just me).

it has been designated SCP-####-2

I'd change it to SCP-####-1 since you never mentioned -1.

with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED]

I don't understand why this is redacted. I'd recommend reading this guide

I just happen to be in the wrong place

You don't need to change this since dialogue doesn't have to have perfect grammar, but "happen" should be "happened"

Subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####. Immediately, SCP-#### began activating, and subject disappeared from the cell.

I'd change this to "SCP-#### activated immediately after subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####." You can remove "subject disappeared from the cell" because the next couple sentences imply that the subject disappeared.

Subject 6 was found to have transported to a closed doorway, and suffered [DATA EXPUNGED]. Subject died █ minutes after initial recovery.

I'd change this to "Subject 6 was found to have been transported inside of a closed doorway and could not be recovered." Saying that they couldn't be recovered implies that they were located but died before they could be properly rescued.

item.title: Re: Carnivorous Tattoo
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the criticism, I appreciate it.

Unfortunately due to the fact there is a 400 word limit from what I’ve been told and read for these posts I can’t put alot of details in without going over the limit so I’ll answer your questions here! So in Order:

  • I was thinking a possible minor memetic ability it has causes the host prey have false memories of getting the tattoo in order to lull the prey host into a false belief.
  • Basically what i mean is that more tattoos would appear on the prey hosts body taking the form of claw/bite marks like one would see on a carcass after a animal chews and claws at it.
  • On the outside the victim looks completely fine with no physical wounds anywhere on the body save for the tatto markings. Autopsy however would show that random organs/muscle tissue seemed to have mysteriously vanished with no answers as to how and what caused it. This is what also caught the attention of the foundation.
  • The Tattoo appears randomly, ranging from a few minutes to days before its next manifestation as well as its victims being random as well with no pattern being apparent.
  • i have the scp set up in a way it favors more exotic predators such as extinct ones as a means of attracting more prey since the more intricate a tattoo the more it would attract tattoo enthusiasts.
  • Basically its hunting style would be similar to species that try to disorient/separate prey in an attempt to get the host to leave the sight of anyone around them so it can strike.

item.title: The Zenwalker (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
A tragic complex story of a powerful entity playing hero only to become the only threat he ever had to worry about.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Cosmic Horror, Drama/Emotional,

Page Layout (Optional): This is going to be a rare case of and scp article in an scp article. There will be the normal containment procedures followed by a description then an addendum containing an scp article about this scp that he brought with him from the future (I know, bare with me). After the addendum, logs reviewing the interviews with the scp.

Elevator Pitch: Basically, this scp is an anomalous man from a different dimension in which the laws of physics are fundamentally different. It's because of this difference that he has the ability to manipulate gravity. His upbringing and childlike curiosity provided the perfect origin story for a modern superhero with a scientific alter ego. By day he was a lab coat pushing the limits of his abilities to fully understand gravity and it's effects, by night a merciless vigilante obliterating local crime with an iron fist.

+ show block
– hide block

Now, I know what it looks like but stay with me, this isn't just another superhero. In fact, the true danger of this scp came from his day job as a scientist. His continuous experiments yielded amazing discoveries about what he could do, but it eventually led to the collapse of the universe as we know it. The collapse of the universe damned him to just exist in an existence in which he was the only thing that excited. Madness had claimed him after a millennia of solitude, but he didn't spend his time in the void laying down. He used this time to further study his ability. Eventually he was able to feel the connection between time and gravity. This led his ability to manipulate time. From there he formulated a plan to send himself back in time to kill his younger self before he collapses the universe. However, do to his mental instability he was slain his younger self. That younger version of himself grew to repeat history/the future and collapsed the universe, went mad, discovered time travel, and repeated the plan to kill his younger self. This time however, he remembered how he defeated his older self and didn't fall for the same tactic he used when he was younger. This caused the fight to last a while longer than the first fight. However, the younger version of himself still came out on top do to his mental edge. This younger version of himself repeated the same cycle extending the fight just a bit longer. As the cycle continued the scale of the battle grew larger, so did the foundation's involvement. This only served to escalate the situation as it eventually led to a broken masquerade. This cycle repeated until the battle was the cause of the collapsed universe. The cycle finally ended when he decided to instead travel farther back in time and seek out the foundation to contain his younger self before he grows up to become a threat. The conversation with a mad man didn't get nearly as far as the scp article he brought back with him as proof of his claims. The article inside the article is the one he brought back with him and the over all article will be the whole story.

Central Narrative: It's a tragic story of a hero being his only threat. Eventually ending the narrative before it starts.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The very deeply rooted story.

Additional Notes: This is my first attribution to the site in general and I'm sure I have a lot to learn. This is me diving head first into a community I've loved for years and should have contributed to ages ago. All criticism welcome and appreciated.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 130 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

Shouldn't the several hundred additional entities receive SCP designations? Shouldn't the Foundation perhaps take an interest in establishing communication with this species, if only in order to negotiate a less Veil-endangering place for them to portal in next time?

The Foundation presented in this scip seems amateurish and sloppy. Even compliant sentient entities are nontrivial to contain. It doesn't help that we're just offhandedly told that the second round of containment was successful, easy peasy, as if the evaluator is carefree and disinterested. There isn't even a cliché note about administering amnestics to witnesses.

I guess I'm in the minority, given that the article has 150+ upvotes. It's not all bad. I like the anomaly itself. I think its use of Yelp is cute, in a good way. But even the more cringe-inducing articles of the LOLFoundation era don't present this cavalier an institution.

From here spores will begin to fly out of SCP-XXXX-1, which will multiply SCP-XXXX

One of my absolute favorite SCPs. There's just enough there to piece together the narrative, and it's a good narrative. And it easily has one of the best first person descents into madness I've seen in any horror story, and I've seen a lot of those.

Some possibly spoilery thoughts:

+ show block
– hide block

I interpret the light as destroying the metaphysical "anchor" that keeps something squarely in a single reality, making it exist in multiple parallel realities at once, maybe even every possible reality at once. That's why the researcher says they're not ready for "what's out there"; every possible reality in the Foundation's carefully monitored test chambers is much easier to deal with than the chaos of the world outside. This idea fits in with Star Signals, which describes the Fifth World as your ideal version of reality, the universe sculpted by you into your perfect shape. By severing your connection to one single world, the light gives you the freedom to move to any world. But the human mind isn't made for this, and very strange things happen to a person when they do this.

Most assume the 'body' referred to in "Don't worry about the body" must be a corpse, but I think that line should actually be taken as a much more general statement. As in, don't worry about the physical body, the mind is what matters. Given 3005's general effects on human bodies, this seems like solid advice.

Honestly, I love this SCP, along with 1425, so much that I have trouble accepting any other take on the Fifth Church into my personal headcanon, which I suppose is ironic given the subject material.

I am really teetering on the edge of an upvote for this one. To be clear, I really like the story itself, but…

The one problem I have with this is that I just can't see the Foundation letting any of this happen. I can buy the doctors being sassy as all hell, because, they kinda work in an actual hellscape and humour is a major coping mechanism. The problem I do have is that the Foundation isn't incompetent and is very strict about following the rules (at least in my headcannon). That whole section charter quote, in my headcannon, is not a slap on the wrist kind of violation (did she even get that much?). For me, that would be grounds for immediate and pretty severe disciplinary action.

As I said, I like the story, so it's not even close to a downvote, but this just really messes with how I view the Foundation (and not in a good way). Ah well, I hope this opinion isn't completely outlandish to you. I look forward to seeing more (and hopefully upvoting next time)
